cohort: 2598 childbearing women and their newborns at a clinical hospital in Santiago, Chile
finding: Immigrant women had better maternal and neonatal indicators compared to native Chilean women, including lower rates of obesity, caesarean section, obstetric morbidity, pre-eclampsia, gestational diabetes, and prematurity.
mod_finding: Immigrant women had a significantly lower rate of cesarean section compared to native-born women (31.7% vs. 36.8%).
